title: SRT3 Overview
description: Home screen: is everything up, how hard is it working, what does it cost. Click any host bar to drill down.

panels.title: Active alerts
panels.description: Alerts currently firing (critical + warning). These also push to your iPhone through Home Assistant. Click to open the alert list.

panels.title: Cluster power
panels.description: Viper + Hellcat + Demon, from the HS300 outlets. Sparkline = trend over the time range.

panels.title: Cluster cost / month
panels.description: Projected: current draw x 720 h x $0.45/kWh (PG&E blended). Change the rate in /etc/prometheus/rules/srt3-records.yml.

panels.title: Internet ping
panels.description: Best round-trip to Cloudflare / Google from Hellcat. AT&T fiber is normally 3-15 ms.

panels.title: Packet loss (5 min)
panels.description: Share of internet pings that got no reply in the last 5 minutes.

panels.title: 10G fabric traffic
panels.description: Sum of rx+tx on all NICs negotiated at 10 Gbit/s (Mellanox CX312B on the CRS305).

panels.title: Up / down history
panels.description: Green = answering, red = not. Hosts come from Prometheus scrapes; services from HTTP checks every 30s; internet from pings. Ryzenous and Ollama go red whenever the desktop sleeps - that's expected.

panels.title: Hosts  (click a bar to drill into that host)
CPU busy
panels.description: Share of CPU time not idle, averaged over all cores, last 2 min.

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: RAM in use (excludes reclaimable cache). On Proxmox this includes VM memory.

panels.title: Root disk used
panels.description: / on Linux, C: on Ryzenous. An alert fires if the trend says it'll be full within 7 days.

panels.title: Hottest sensor
panels.description: Highest hwmon reading per host (CPU package, NVMe, etc). M920q throttles near 100 °C.

panels.title: CPU busy over time
panels.description: Recorded every 30s by a recording rule, so this panel is cheap no matter the time range.

panels.title: Memory used over time
panels.description: Bytes in use per host. Hellcat (16 GB) runs the Home Assistant VM plus this monitoring stack.

panels.title: Package updates pending
panels.description: apt packages with updates available, per Proxmox host (refreshed by a Debian timer every few hours).

panels.title: NVMe wear
panels.description: SMART 'percentage used': how far through its rated write life each boot SSD is.

panels.title: Failed services
panels.description: systemd units in the failed state on any Proxmox host, shown as host · unit. Host Detail lists them too.

panels.title: Reboot needed
panels.description: Hosts that installed a kernel/lib update and need a reboot to finish it.

panels.title: Ping, hop by hop
panels.description: Round-trip from Hellcat to each hop. If only the internet lines spike, it's the ISP; if the router line spikes too, it's your LAN.

panels.title: Throughput: 10G fabric vs 1G LAN
panels.description: rx+tx per host. 10G = Mellanox port on the CRS305; 1G = onboard NIC to the NicGiga/router.

panels.title: Service response time
panels.description: How long each web UI took to answer the last check (30s interval). Down services show in the timeline above.

panels.title: Busiest NICs right now
panels.description: rx+tx per physical NIC across every host.

panels.title: Power by outlet (HS300)
panels.description: Each HS300 outlet, stacked, so the top edge is the whole strip.

panels.title: Share of strip power (now)
panels.description: Where the watts are going right now.

panels.title: GPU utilization
panels.description: Busy share of the GPU's SMs. LLM inference and Demucs show up here.

panels.title: VRAM used
panels.description: 8 GB card. A loaded Ollama model sits here even when idle.

panels.title: GPU power
panels.description: Board power from nvidia-smi (3070 limit is about 220 W).

panels.title: Firing now
panels.description: Every alert rule currently firing, straight from the ALERTS metric Prometheus keeps. Empty = all good.

options.content:
### How this stack works

**Exporters** are tiny programs on each machine that publish numbers at `http://host:port/metrics`:
`node_exporter` on Viper/Hellcat/Demon (:9100), `windows_exporter` (:9182) and `nvidia_gpu_exporter` (:9835) on Ryzenous,
Home Assistant's `/api/prometheus` for the HS300, and `blackbox_exporter` on Hellcat, which pings and HTTP-checks things on Prometheus's behalf.

**Prometheus** (Hellcat :9090) *scrapes* (pulls) every target every 15-30 s and stores each number as a time series.
Every series has a name and labels, e.g. `node_network_receive_bytes_total{node="viper", device="enp1s0d1"}`.

**PromQL** is the query language. `rate(x[1m])` turns an ever-increasing counter into a per-second speed. `sum by (node)` groups. `x > 0.9` filters.
Hover the (i) on any panel to see what it measures. Click **Edit** on a panel to see its exact query.

**Recording rules** precompute common queries every 30 s into clean `srt3:*` series (e.g. `srt3:cpu_busy:ratio`), so these dashboards stay fast.
**Alert rules** are PromQL conditions with a duration (`for: 5m`). Firing alerts go to **Alertmanager** (:9093), which de-duplicates, groups and sends them to Home Assistant, which pushes them to your phone.

**Grafana** (here) only draws. Try these: drag-select on any graph to zoom; press `Esc` to back out; change the time range top-right;
hover one graph and the crosshair follows on all of them; click a host bar to drill down; the orange/red markers on graphs are reboots and alerts.
Explore (compass icon, left menu) is a blank query scratchpad. Try `srt3:` and let autocomplete show you everything.
